title: Cybersecurity final assessment bank 09

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the main idea of Introduction to DevSecOps?
options: Introduction to DevSecOps focuses on devops and security integration; security responsibilities across development teams; security gates and approval processes. Define the system or data in scope, the expected behavior, and the consequences if that behavior fails. Then select a proportionate control and identify evidence that can verify both the normal path and an important failure case.
A single successful test proves that a system is completely secure in every environment.
The fastest workflow is always to skip evidence collection and make changes directly in production.
Security responsibilities disappear when a technical tool has been installed.
questions.answer_key: Introduction to DevSecOps focuses on devops and security integration; security responsibilities across development teams; security gates and approval processes. Define the system or data in scope, the expected behavior, and the consequences if that behavior fails. Then select a proportionate control and identify evidence that can verify both the normal path and an important failure case.
questions.explanation: The lesson's core idea is: Introduction to DevSecOps focuses on devops and security integration; security responsibilities across development teams; security gates and approval processes. Define the system or data in scope, the expected behavior, and the consequences if that behavior fails. Then select a proportionate control and identify evidence that can verify both the normal path and an important failure case. The other options overstate what one test or tool can prove and ignore the need for context, evidence, and governance.

questions.prompt: Which practice most improves the reliability of work on Dependency and Package Security?
options: Document assumptions and limitations, then select a proportionate defensive next step based on evidence and current guidance.
Publish raw secrets and personal information so someone else can reproduce the test.
Treat a teaching example as proof of production security without retesting.
Skip documenting exceptions because they make the report more complicated.
questions.answer_key: Document assumptions and limitations, then select a proportionate defensive next step based on evidence and current guidance.
questions.explanation: Security claims should be backed by reproducible evidence and clear limits; sensitive information must be protected and production-specific assumptions checked.

questions.prompt: You are applying Software Supply Chain Assurance to a new scenario. What is the best first step?
options: Define scope and expected behavior, collect relevant evidence, and verify the result in an authorized or synthetic environment.
Repeat the same test against unrelated public systems to collect more data.
Disable useful logging so the test output looks simpler.
Assume an unfamiliar result proves malicious intent without corroboration.
questions.answer_key: Define scope and expected behavior, collect relevant evidence, and verify the result in an authorized or synthetic environment.
questions.explanation: Bound the work, define expected behavior, and collect relevant evidence in a safe and authorized context before drawing conclusions.
